items.title: Your Dumont setup now loads
items.description: The desktop app reads the same config as the dumont-code CLI, so team rules, memory, permissions and every shared skill are available here too. Before this it only looked at the stock opencode config and found none of it.

items.title: Provider keys work without a terminal
items.description: Keys come from ~/.config/dumont/llm-keys.env directly, so launching from the Dock or Finder gets the same models as running from a shell.

items.title: No more Unauthorized on your first message
items.description: The app used to default to a model routed through OpenCode Zen, a paid gateway Dumont does not fund, which failed with api_error: Unauthorized. It now picks a provider you actually have a key for.

items.title: You can tell the providers apart
items.description: Two models could both show as deepseek-v4-flash, one of which would never work. Anything routed through Zen is now labelled, so the model you pick is the model you get.

items.title: The login page is Dumont Code
items.description: Signing in to a provider used to land on a page branded opencode. It is ours now, wordmark and all.

items.title: Dumont Code
items.description: The desktop app is now Dumont Code: its own name, icon, bundle id and dumontcode:// scheme. opencode:// keeps working, because the server and CLI still emit those deep links.

items.title: Updates come from Dumont
items.description: The updater and the release notes you are reading both point at dumont.au. Nothing in the app can pull a build from an upstream host any more.

items.title: A Dumont theme, light and dark
items.description: Navy and teal, on by default, and built so light mode is the good one rather than an afterthought. Every upstream theme is still in the picker.

items.title: Signed and notarised
items.description: Apple Developer ID signed, notarised and stapled, so it opens on first launch with no trip through Privacy & Security.

items.title: Apple silicon and Intel
items.description: Separate arm64 and x64 downloads, both signed, both fed by the same update channel.
